kt (Customer): Hey team — we got a sudden burst this morning ~14:12 UTC: ~30s of very high RPS and then a flood of 429s. Also noticed an unexpected billing blip. We were expecting burst credits to smooth short spikes — can you explain why requests were rejected so quickly?

maya (Support): Sorry about that, kt. We can dig in. Quick questions: do you have dedicated capacity or hosted API usage? Any client-side concurrency changes or deploys around the time? Can you attach a couple request IDs / sample response headers you saw?

kt (Customer): Hosted API. No deploys. Client concurrency went from ~10 to ~80 for ~20s when a job retried aggressively. One sample response header: `x-rwinf-retry-after: 2` and `x-rwinf-burst-remaining: 0`. Request id: rwinf_20260315_abc123. Billing spike: +$40 for that minute compared to baseline.

aj (SRE): Thanks — that header `x-rwinf-burst-remaining: 0` is the key. Short version: we have a leaky-bucket style burst pool per project that smooths short spikes. It replenishes at a steady rate. If a very short, very high concurrency wave drains the pool, subsequent requests are rate-limited until credits refill.

aj (SRE): More detail: the burst credits are meant for short, infrequent spikes. They allow extra throughput for a short time, but they aren't infinite. When the pool is exhausted we return 429 with retry info. The billing jump can happen because tokens still consumed for accepted requests (and some retries).

ryan (Eng): To check timeline on our end, can you run a quick repro so we can see headers across a sweep? Example stress curl (safe, single-host test):

```bash
for i in {1..60}; do curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY' \\ \\  -X POST \\ \\  -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done; wait
```

ryan (Eng): If you run that with concurrency, you should see `x-rwinf-burst-remaining` drop to 0 and then `x-rwinf-retry-after` start appearing. Please only run against a non-prod key or let us know first.

maya (Support): For troubleshooting, please attach: a few request IDs (you already gave one), approximate RPS timeline (per-minute), and any client retry settings. We'll pull our quota/burst timeline for the project and correlate.

kt (Customer): RPS timeline: 10/min baseline, spike to ~300/min for 25s, then back to 12/min. Client retried 3x with no jitter. I can share a short HAR.

aj (SRE): That pattern (very dense retries + no jitter) drains bursts fast. Two immediate mitigations: 1) Add client-side exponential backoff + jitter to avoid synchronized retries. 2) Limit concurrency on the client so you never exceed a known safe level.

aj (SRE): Longer-term options: increase your quota (makes burst pool larger), or switch to Dedicated/reserved capacity if you expect regular high short spikes. We can also enable a smoothing policy on your account that spreads short excess over a slightly longer window — effectively a larger leaky bucket with a slower refill so you get fewer 429s but potentially slightly higher per-minute cost.

sophie (Acct Mgmt): For the billing blip, if the traffic pattern was a one-off short spike we can review and potentially apply a goodwill credit if it looks like a single, unusual event. Please confirm timestamps and the project id and I'll open a billing review.

kt (Customer): Project id: proj_zz_topsecret. Spike window UTC 14:11:58 - 14:12:23. Sending HAR and request IDs in DM.

maya (Support): Got it. We're pulling the burst-credit consumption graph now. One note on headers you'll see: `x-rwinf-burst-remaining` (credits left), `x-rwinf-burst-replenish-ms` (ms until the pool is top-up by one unit), and `Retry-After` or `x-rwinf-retry-after` which is advisory. If you want to make your client more resilient, check for either 429 + these headers and apply backoff.

ryan (Eng): Example client pseudo-code for robust retry (very common):

```python
import random, time

def backoff(attempt):
    base = 0.2
    return base * (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 0.1)

# on 429 or 503
# sleep(backoff(attempt)) and then retry up to N
```

aj (SRE): Also note: enabling smoothing means your accepted requests may be slowed fractionally rather than rejected. For latency-sensitive workloads that is sometimes worse than a 429+fast retry. So pick based on client behavior. If your client can retry quickly with jitter, 429s are fine. If you can't tolerate retries, smoothing helps.

kt (Customer): Is there a console toggle for smoothing?

ryan (Eng): There's a per-project toggle in Console -> Projects -> Quotas -> Burst smoothing (beta) — we can flip it for you and monitor. If you want, we can enable it for 24h and watch the effect.

maya (Support): From support ops: we'll pull the exact credit burn graph and attach it here. Also check if your client is leaking tokens or rapidly spawning workers — we've seen hidden retry loops in job frameworks that widened small blips into bigger ones.

billing-bot: Billing alert: project proj_zz_topsecret exceeded expected minute spend by 1800% at 1765500000. Invoice segment flagged for review.

sophie (Acct Mgmt): I'm on billing review. If this is a one-off, we'll handle it; if it's recurring due to traffic patterns we should discuss quota bump or reserved capacity.

kt (Customer): Appreciate it. Please flip smoothing for 24h and pull the graphs — I'll add jitter and reduce concurrency asap. Thanks.

aj (SRE): Done — enabled burst smoothing for 24h. We'll post the before/after charts here in ~10–15m. Also we're correlating request ids now. If you can, send a small reproduction run after you apply jitter so we can confirm behavior.

maya (Support): Closing loop steps we'll do: 1) attach credit burn chart, 2) confirm smoothing toggle, 3) billing review with acct mgmt, 4) guidance snippet for client retry (copy above).

kt (Customer): Sounds good — sending HAR and logs DM now. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:

aj (SRE): Chart posted: `burst_credits_time_series.png` (internal link). You can see the pool hit 0 at 14:12:05 and stayed drained for ~40s before refill. That aligns with the 429s. We'll leave the smoothing toggle on as requested and follow up tomorrow with a short postmortem note.

maya (Support): If anything else pops up ping me directly.

kt (Customer): Thanks — very helpful.
